page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 3.6 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is a key highlight, featuring 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 95,190.03 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 22,291.0, both placing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is notable, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 6,647.5 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 119.86 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 33,739.36 and Redis SET performance of 117.71 million operations per second. Additionally, the CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix mathematics, which assists in prompt processing for medium and large language models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.metal-24xl offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with high-speed DDR5 memory on a bare-metal platform, reducing virtualization overhead. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks falling in the average tier, indicating that workloads relying on single-threaded execution may not fully leverage this hardware. This server is suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput data warehousing, real-time analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications requiring direct physical access to hardware.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server designed for data-intensive workloads. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory and a massive 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supported by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and strong database operations throughput, alongside hardware-accelerated matrix extensions (AMX). While single-core performance remains average, the server's large storage capacity and high memory density make it qualitatively cost-efficient for bare-metal deployments. It is suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
